01 · Executive summary

The verdict in two minutes

LokAI's substance already outruns most 2026 portfolio apps; its surface is missing the last 5% that makes reviewers feel it. The design-system governance (semantic tokens, enforced contrast gates, motion doctrine, bilingual script system) is recruiter-grade evidence of systems thinking — the #1 2026 hiring signal. The gaps are concentrated, small, and fixable in about one focused day: press feedback, safe-area hardening, a desktop dark-mode path, OKLCH, and four one-line motion/typography corrections.

What already competes (keep, and lead the case study with it)

✓ Token architecture "named by job, never by hue", enforced repo-wide by verify:demo gates (C-16)
✓ Reduced-motion philosophy: "a gentler equivalent, not zero feedback" (C-03)
✓ One entrance recipe, springs reserved for user-summoned surfaces — "overshoot on a refusal would be unearned" (C-05, C-08)
✓ EN/HI/MR/TA script-aware typography with documented font rationale (C-19, C-21)
✓ AI trust surfaces matching the 2026 bar: grounded claims, stop states, human-review gates (market §4)

What is lacking (ranked by recruiter feel)

1 · No press physics — a paper-metaphor UI where nothing compresses (C-10 FAIL, both platforms)
2 · Mobile-native hardening missing — safe areas, tap highlight, 16px inputs, 100vh (C-30 FAIL)
3 · Dark mode unreachable on desktop — built, gated… then wired mobile-only (C-17)
4 · sRGB pipeline under a modern token story (C-18 FAIL)
5 · Small canonical misses — one ease-in, one layout-anim, 60ms stagger, 32px icon buttons, no text-wrap/smoothing (C-02/05/07/13/19)

Mobile

20 PASS · 8 PARTIAL · 4 FAIL · 3 N/A. The five-slot screen grammar (32/16px, 44px taps, 50px CTA) is a quiet strength; phone-native basics are the blind spot.

Desktop

19 PASS · 8 PARTIAL · 4 FAIL · 4 N/A. The two-tone paper-desk world reads authored; the dark-mode dead path and 32px icon buttons are what a senior reviewer catches first.

Effort to close

~1 focused day for all 7 hard gaps (each is one-liner-to-one-afternoon, gate-verifiable via the repo's own verify:demo). Roadmap in §8.

02 · Method & evidence integrity

How this audit was produced

StepWhat actually happened
Library ingestionAll 10 files in the skills folder read in full; every distinct rule extracted and translated into 35 verdict-able criteria (C-01…C-35), 9 internal contradictions flagged (not silently resolved), and a 16-rule × 3-platform matrix built. Full catalog: skill-catalog.md
Screen evidence13 live screenshots captured from the running dev build (Edge headless, light theme, 1440×900 ×6 and 390×844 ×7) — embedded below in §5/§6.
Vision limitation (disclosed)The image-understanding model was unavailable for this entire session (provider 400/403 on 6+ attempts with backoff). Visual findings therefore come from deterministic pixel quantization (palette extraction per screen, reproducible from palette-analysis.txt) plus code inspection — not full visual comprehension. Aesthetic judgments that genuinely need eyes (alignment drift, optical spacing) are marked low-confidence rather than guessed.
Code-level audit20+ deterministic greps/file reads over src/: easing, durations, transitions, tokens, aria, focus, reduced-motion, safe-area, font loading, paste handling, dark-theme wiring. Key counts are re-verified in §10.
Market benchmark11 web queries → 12 screen-visible 2026 trends, 10 ranked recruiter signals, AI-native UX bar, legal-tech trust expectations — 40 sources listed in §10, thin evidence flagged LOW inside §4.
Scoring disciplinePer the catalog: accessibility is a gate, not a theme; verdicts are per-platform (no blended averages); a FAIL in a High-weight criterion caps its theme at PARTIAL; absence of motion can be a PASS; where library files disagree, the stricter number is applied and the conflict noted.
Library contradiction handling: the library disagrees with itself on touch-target floor (40 vs 44 vs 48px), press-scale values, ease-in scope, and font stacks. This audit applies the stricter value and reports the conflict — the full contradiction table is in §3.3.

4.2 Recruiter lens (ranked, sourced)

1 · Shipped, traceable work beats case studies — 2026 senior signal
2 · 2–3 minute skim; ~78% AI-assisted pre-screening — instant legibility
3 · Judgment in messy constraints — not "UX methods exist" proof
4 · Impact hierarchy — lead with outcomes, not artifacts
5 · Live problem-solving comfort · 6 · Systems thinking + craft + research evidence

thefountaininstitute.com · blog.uxfol.io · muz.li · thecrit.co · everydayux.net · uxplaybook.org · uxplanet.org

4.3 AI-native bar (2026)

Table stakes: radical transparency · uncertainty states · human override/HITL · data trust signals · conversational layer beside GUI · consistent output structure.

Differentiators: agentic workflow visualization with checkpoints & escalation · generative/adaptive UI · MX design · ethical personalization · DS governance.

Legal-tech specifically: trust = accuracy + relevance + value; hallucinated case-law is a named public risk → grounding/citations effectively mandatory; multilingual support is an India-market essential (uxdt.nic.in).

smashingmagazine.com · aiuxplayground.com · 925studios.co · agentic-design.ai · factor.law · wiley.law · uxdt.nic.in

Read-across to LokAI: the app already sits on the differentiator side of the AI-native bar (visible grounding, stop states, review gates, bilingual determinism — a legal-tech + India double alignment). What reads dated today: dark-mode-as-option, no press physics, sRGB tokens — exactly the gaps in §7.

5.3 Deep dives (top 5 themes)

1 · Mobile-native hardening missing (C-30). No safe-area insets, no tap-highlight removal, 12px composer text zooms on iOS focus, 100vh in 10 files. A recruiter feels this in 30 seconds on a real phone. One-afternoon fix.

2 · Press feedback lacks the physical cue (C-10). The entire language is "paper on desk" — but controls don't compress. :active{transform:scale(0.97)} + existing MOTION.press closes the loop between philosophy and feel.

3 · 2021-grade color pipeline under 2026-grade tokens (C-18). Semantic roles are exemplary; the values are sRGB. OKLCH migration is mechanical (25 CSS vars) and makes the multi-hue wash system equal-lightness by construction.

4 · Dark mode architecturally ready, UX-fragile (C-17). Role-layer re-theming + both-theme contrast gate exist; preference evaporates on reload. One localStorage read finishes it.

5 · Micro-motion 80% there (C-05/07/13). One ease-in exit, one grid-template-rows animation, 60ms stagger — three single-line fixes from canonical.

5.4 Mobile recruiter verdict (2026)

LokAI mobile reads as systems-thinking evidence, not a dribbble shot — the exact 2026 differentiator. What survives the 2–3 minute skim: a governed token system with enforcement gates, bilingual script-aware typography, and AI trust surfaces that map one-to-one onto the 2026 AI-native bar (transparency, HITL, stop states). Legal-tech grounding answers the field's #1 demand.

What holds it back on first touch: the experience feels less physical than its own philosophy (no press scale), misses phone-native basics a senior reviewer checks in seconds, and its restraint can read as timidity next to 2026's expressive baseline unless the case study frames restraint as the trust-design choice.

Top 5 standout gaps: safe-area/input-zoom hardening · press physics · dark-mode fragility · sRGB pipeline · unexplained Files-screen darkness.
5 quickest wins: press-scale one-liner · safe-area padding · 16px composer · toast ease swap · localStorage persistence — roughly one focused day, all gate-verifiable.

6.3 Deep dives + recruiter verdict (2026)

1 · Dark mode is architecturally complete but desktop-dead (C-17). Re-tuned role layer, both-theme contrast gate — all built, then wired mobile-only. A reviewer on a dark-OS laptop sees a light-only app; 2026 sources call dark mode a baseline. ~10 lines to fix.
2 · The physical metaphor lacks its final cue (C-10) — same as mobile, system-wide.
3 · sRGB under a semantic-role story (C-18).
4 · Icon buttons under-size (C-02): 32px in Chat.
5 · Editorial typography missing its last 5% (C-19/C-27): balance, smoothing, scroll-margin — three one-liners.

Verdict: the first impression is authorship — a two-tone paper-desk world with an evidence-first workflow, mapping directly onto the 2026 standout signals (systems thinking, DS governance, AI-native trust, shipped-and-traceable). What undercuts it: the desktop dark-mode dead path (30-second notice), static press feel, 32px targets, sRGB. None structural; four of five are one-line or one-afternoon fixes. With them, desktop sits credibly beside Linear/Vercel-grade 2026 products on feel while its governance story already outranks most on substance.

09 · Recruiter one-pager

Detach this and walk into the interview

The two-minute read

LokAI is a working, deterministic AI legal-guide prototype with enforcement-gated design governance — a portfolio piece that answers the three questions a 2026 design hiring manager actually asks: Can this person build systems, not just screens? Can they design AI people trust? Does the work survive contact with a real phone?

Standout evidence (lead with these):

① A token architecture "named by job, never by hue", enforced by repository scripts that fail the build on violations — design law as executable code (systems thinking, the #1 signal).
② AI-native trust surfaces built to the 2026 bar: visible grounding (groundedClaims/totalClaims, never fake percentages), tiered stop states that refuse unsafe next steps, human-review gates before anything leaves the app (transparency + HITL + escalation — exactly the smashingmagazine/agentic-design differentiators).
③ Legal-AI grounding discipline in the field where hallucinated citations are a named public risk (factor.law, wiley.law).
④ Four-script typography (EN/HI/MR/TA) with script-aware line-heights and a documented anti-generic font rationale — an India-market alignment the government's own UX guidelines call essential.
⑤ Shipped-and-traceable: every design decision has a doc, a token, and a gate — the 2026 senior signal.

Honest gaps (name them before the reviewer does): press physics, mobile-native hardening, desktop dark-mode wiring, OKLCH — all identified in this audit, all with dated fixes in the roadmap, all closeable in ~1 day. Say: "I audited it against a 35-criteria skills library and the 2026 market; here's the gap list and the fix queue." That sentence itself is the differentiator.

Skip-triggers to avoid (uxplaybook/uxplanet): missing metrics, fluff, no CTA. Attach the live demo link, the graph of the design system (graphify-out), and this report's roadmap as the "what I'd do next" page.

Quickest wins (impact ÷ effort)

1. Press scale one-liner (C-10) · 2. Safe-area + 16px composer (C-30) · 3. Desktop theme provider + toggle (C-17) · 4. Toast ease swap (C-05) · 5. text-wrap:balance on headlines (C-19). Combined: one focused day, every fix provable via verify:demo.

Where it already beats the market

Governance depth (scripted gates are rare in portfolios), trust-surface completeness vs the AI-native table-stakes list, bilingual scope, and a coherent authored visual language (C-34 PASS on both platforms) — the thing 2026 trend-chasing apps most often lack.
